title: Shift Command J closes an open path
goal: Closing a path drawn with the Pen today means finding Close Path in a menu, because Shift Command J is New Layer via Cut. That command only does anything with a marquee up, so when an open path is picked and no marquee is up, let Shift Command J close the path, as the icon success list asks.
notes: icon-vector success item 1: 'every anchor and handle stays draggable, and Shift Cmd J closes the path'. Open thread in manager report 2026-10-08-0639: 'Close Path has no key (Shift Cmd J is New Layer via Cut)'. Today: EditorCommands.swift:1745 New Layer via Cut, .keyboardShortcut("j", [.command,.shift]), disabled unless canCutSelectionToLayer (needs a marquee). Close Path is the retitled Turn Into Path row (EditorCommands.swift ~1825-1837, turnSelectionIntoPathMenuItem; EditorState+LayerOps.swift:634 Close Path; PathClosing.swift). Pattern for a key that moves by context: the timed ? shortcut : nil idiom at EditorCommands.swift:1359. Photoshop parity memory: keep Photoshop's meaning wherever Photoshop has one, which is why the marquee case keeps New Layer via Cut.
acceptance: At Next defaults, draw an open path with the Pen, switch to Select with it picked and no marquee up, press Shift Command J: the path closes on its own two ends in one undo step
With a marquee up on a picture, Shift Command J is still New Layer via Cut, exactly as before
The menu bar shows Shift Command J against whichever of the two rows it will run right now, never against both at once
A walk covering both cases runs green at Next defaults
If the two rows cannot share the key cleanly, stop, open a decision card on where Close Path's key goes, and mark this task blocked
Audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Adversarial review before building: Photoshop's Shift Cmd J (New Layer via Cut) needs a marquee, Illustrator's Cmd J closes/joins; so a marquee is the whole test and the key keeps Photoshop's meaning whenever one is up. With neither case the key stays printed on the dimmed cut row, where a Photoshop hand looks. The key runs the same Close Path row, so it asks the same question (with Don't ask again); left as an evaluate question in the audit rather than a quiet behaviour change.

Built: PathClose.shiftCommandJ(marqueeUp:closesOnePath:) in PhotonzCore (tests first, PathClosingTests); EditorState.shiftCommandJ + shiftCommandJClosesRow; Layer menu prints the key on exactly one of New Layer via Cut / Close Path…, and the layer row's right-click Close Path… prints it when the key would run that row. Walk shift-command-j-closes-a-path-walk needs front:true: in a background walk the menu bar is frozen at launch (the row read Turn Into Path… and the key sat on the cut), measured on the first run. Green at Next defaults; neighbour walks close-an-open-path, cut-onto-its-own-layer, mirror-across-center x2 green; Scripts/test.sh 12012 tests green.
